subject: Window seats with integrated storage
hook: Do I need a bay window to have a window seat?
fb:
"Do I need a bay window to have a window seat?"

Not at all. A bay is the classic spot, but a seat works under a flat window, between two wardrobes or alcove units, on a wide landing, or as a bench in a kitchen-diner. As long as there's enough wall width and the window can still open, we can usually make something work.

Got an unusual window in mind? Ask us below or arrange a free design consultation.

gbp:
"Do I need a bay window to have a window seat?"

No. Bay windows are the classic place for one, but a window seat with storage can work under a standard flat window, in a deep window reveal, between two wardrobes or alcove units, on a wide landing, or as built-in bench seating in a kitchen-diner.

What matters is having enough wall width for a comfortable seat, room for the window and blinds to open, and a plan for anything below the window, such as a radiator or sockets.

At a free, no-obligation design consultation we measure the window and wall, talk through how you'll use the seat, and suggest drawers, lift-up storage or a mix. Each seat is made in our Hanley workshop and fitted by our own team.

Book a consultation and send us a photo of the window you have in mind.

Q: Do I need a bay window for a window seat? |
A: No. Bays are the classic spot, but a seat works under any window with enough wall width, between two alcove or wardrobe units, or across a deep window reveal. Bedrooms, landings and kitchen-diners all suit one. We measure the wall and window, then design the seat and storage around them.
